interventions.body: Postoperative prognosis depends on the preoperative PSA and the prostatectomy findings. Extraprostatic extension is reported absent. Positive surgical margins is reported absent. Seminal vesicle invasion is reported absent. Lymphovascular invasion is reported absent. Postoperative PSA and its subsequent trajectory are needed to refine this prognosis; a future recurrence date cannot be established from surgical risk factors alone. The fixed estimated horizon is 62.29 months. This represents expected follow-up without an event, not a known recurrence date. The sensitivity range is 46.72–77.86 months; its coverage has not been validated.

attempts.text: The postoperative pathology demonstrates a Gleason 4+3 (ISUP grade group 3) diagnosis with pathological stage pT2c. Favorable findings include negative surgical margins, absence of seminal vesicle invasion, and no lymph node metastasis, as documented by the surgical pathology report: "The robot-assisted radical prostatectomy specimen showed Gleason 4+3 (ISUP grade group 3), pathological stage pT2c. There was no extraprostatic extension; surgical margins were negative; the seminal vesicles were not invaded; lymphovascular invasion was absent; there was no lymph node metastasis." The biopsy findings showed Gleason 3+4 in the peripheral zone, with the second biopsy identifying Gleason 3+4 without cribriform pattern or intraductal carcinoma. Countervailing findings are limited as no adverse nodal status was documented, and the absence of lymphovascular invasion is reassuring. The prognosis is influenced by the documented negative margins and absence of nodal metastasis. However, the postoperative PSA is not recorded, meaning biochemical recurrence cannot be assessed. Missing nodal sampling, although not applicable here as nodes were sampled, generally widens uncertainty in staging. Postoperative PSA and its subsequent trajectory are critical information that would revise this prognosis.

The surgical pathology report indicates "surgical margins were negative; the seminal vesicles were not invaded; lymphovascular invasion was absent; there was no lymph node metastasis." This is a reassuring finding regarding local and regional disease control. The preoperative findings included a Gleason 4+3 (ISUP grade group 3) and pathological stage pT2c. The biopsy findings showed Gleason 3+4 in the peripheral zone, with no cribriform pattern or intraductal carcinoma identified in the second session. The absence of lymph node metastasis is a positive prognostic factor. Countervailing findings are limited as no adverse extension or positive margins were documented. Postoperative PSA is not recorded, so biochemical recurrence cannot be assessed. Missing nodal sampling is not a factor here as nodes were sampled, but generally widens uncertainty in staging.
